newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was generally lower on fairly good demand and moderate to heavy offerings this week, USDA said.
Retail demand for immediate needs was somewhat disappointing following the holiday, but very good forward interest was noted for mid-to-late July and early August.

Rib and loin cuts traded lower throughout the trading period with the Select cuts under the heaviest pressure. Round cuts traded at steady levels most of the trading period. Most chuck cuts incurred gradual increases with an exception being Choice chuck rolls, which experienced a notable increase.

Closely trimmed items traded mostly lower, especially loin cuts, on good demand as these cuts were seen as good values. Beef trimmings traded on a firm note early in the week and maintained that level the remaining of the trading period on fairly good demand and mostly moderate offerings.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items traded lower on moderate demand and moderate to heavy offerings.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 4.50 to 8.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal 1.00 to 1.50 higher; Select and Choice round primal steady to 1.00 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 5.00 to 9.00 lower; Closely trimmed item's 1.00 to 2.50 lower; Beef trimmings 1.00 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items 2.00 to 4.00 lower.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.46 at 99.26; 700/850 Dn 1.33 at 99.04; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 2.91 at 92.76; 700/850 Dn 1.83 at 92.51.

COW and BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The lean boneless beef market was firm early as buyers secured product after the announcement of the National School Lunch beef buy. However, as the week progressed, prices weakened on moderate offerings and light demand. The 85% and 65% lean boneless beef traded higher as fast food grinding demand was good throughout the week.

The cow carcass market was steady on moderate demand and offerings. The 100% lean items moved at firm price levels on moderate demand and light to moderate offerings. The tenderloin market was lower late in the week as demand was light.

Utility steady and Cutter carcasses not established; 90% boneless beef unevenly steady; 85% 1.50-2.00 higher; 75% generally steady; 65% 2.00-4.50 higher. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, July 10, 1997 was estimated at 81.16 per cwt., down .42 from a week ago Thursday.
